players.product: SiC MOSFETs and GaN devices for 800V HVDC AI power

quarterly_data.signal: FY2026 (April 2025 - March 2026) results: net sales JPY 481,148 million, up 7.3% year on year, on higher sales in the automotive, consumer and industrial equipment markets; operating income JPY 10,864 million (FY2025: operating loss JPY 40,061 million), helped by higher sales and the fixed-cost savings of the prior year's structural reform; operating margin 2.3% (FY2025: -8.9%); ordinary profit JPY 19,222 million (FY2025: ordinary loss JPY 29,698 million). Net loss attributable to owners of the parent was JPY 158,424 million (FY2025: net loss JPY 50,065 million) after large impairment losses, mainly on SiC business fixed assets. EBITDA (operating income plus depreciation) JPY 67,890 million, up 56.6%.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 net sales JPY 481,148 million (+7.3%); operating income JPY 10,864 million; net loss JPY 158,424 million

quarterly_data.signal: SiC impairment: because the growth outlook for the battery electric vehicle (BEV) market came in below the company's earlier assumption, Rohm booked large impairment losses centred on SiC business fixed assets in FY2026. Total impairment losses were JPY 193,600 million, of which JPY 191,648 million in the Semiconductor Devices segment (FY2025 total: JPY 30,367 million).
quarterly_data.figure: impairment JPY 193,600 million (Semiconductor Devices JPY 191,648 million)

quarterly_data.signal: FY2026 segment results (external sales): LSI net sales JPY 218,390 million (+7.1%), segment profit JPY 24,535 million (FY2025: loss JPY 767 million) - automotive ADAS products were in adjustment but body and xEV high-value products grew, industrial showed a recovery trend, amusement products were firm and server products showed signs of recovery. Semiconductor Devices net sales JPY 205,263 million (+9.7%), segment loss JPY 22,704 million (FY2025: loss JPY 45,899 million) - SiC power device sales for automotive xEV products held firm, Si power devices for automotive and industrial were firm, discretes and LEDs improved on industrial, and semiconductor laser sales for computer and storage grew. Modules net sales JPY 31,589 million (-3.0%), segment profit JPY 3,522 million (+30.9%) - printheads for office equipment rose, automotive LED modules fell. Other (resistors) net sales JPY 25,903 million (+3.5%), segment profit JPY 4,104 million (+62.6%).
quarterly_data.figure: LSI JPY 218,390 million (+7.1%); Semiconductor Devices JPY 205,263 million (+9.7%), loss JPY 22,704 million

quarterly_data.signal: FY2026 orders: orders received JPY 537,555 million (+25.2%) and order backlog JPY 224,634 million (+33.5%) at fiscal year-end. By segment: Semiconductor Devices orders JPY 242,942 million (+40.6%), backlog JPY 114,631 million (+49.0%); LSI orders JPY 236,689 million (+18.6%), backlog JPY 89,772 million (+25.6%); Modules orders JPY 31,376 million (+0.3%), backlog JPY 12,375 million (-1.7%); Other orders JPY 26,547 million (+3.8%), backlog JPY 7,855 million (+8.9%).
quarterly_data.figure: orders JPY 537,555 million (+25.2%); backlog JPY 224,634 million (+33.5%)

quarterly_data.signal: FY2026 production (valued at average selling prices): total JPY 479,890 million (+10.2%); LSI JPY 220,110 million (+10.4%), Semiconductor Devices JPY 201,681 million (+11.6%), Modules JPY 32,156 million (+2.1%), Other JPY 25,942 million (+8.5%). Inventory turnover was 5.45 months at FY2026 year-end versus 6.17 months a year earlier.

Management's view of FY2026 markets: the automotive market came in below the initial view but stayed firm; the industrial equipment market turned to recovery as supply-chain inventory was worked down; consumer demand for amusement products grew sharply; computer and storage stayed firm, centred on servers. Management states it has kept capital expenditure to the necessary minimum to curb fixed-cost growth and has pursued negotiations to pass higher raw material and other costs through into prices, under structural reforms (production site reorganisation, business portfolio optimisation, price optimisation) and making the SiC business profitable.

Second Medium-Term Management Plan "MOVING FORWARD to 2028" (announced November 2025) financial targets for the plan's final year, fiscal 2028 in the company's own numbering (FY2029, the year ending March 2029; the company calls the year ended March 2026 fiscal 2025): net sales of JPY 500 billion or more, operating profit 20% or more, and ROE of 9% or more. The company states that, to raise its international competitiveness, it is weighing options including business portfolio review, stronger technology development and securing business scale through management integration.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2029 (company fiscal 2028) targets: net sales JPY 500 billion or more; operating profit 20% or more; ROE 9% or more

quarterly_data.signal: Material contract: on March 27, 2026 Rohm signed a basic agreement with Toshiba, Japan Industrial Partners, TBJ Holdings and Mitsubishi Electric to start discussions on a business and management integration of Rohm, the semiconductor business of Toshiba Electronic Devices & Storage (a Toshiba subsidiary) and Mitsubishi Electric's power device business. The company states it will pursue the talks to reach a business scale and technology base able to compete in the world market.

FY2026 capital expenditure JPY 82,403 million (-38.1%), of which Semiconductor Devices JPY 69,099 million, LSI JPY 8,351 million, Modules JPY 829 million, Other JPY 979 million and shared sales / administration JPY 3,143 million (FY2025: JPY 133,017 million; FY2024: JPY 186,755 million). Depreciation JPY 57,026 million (FY2025: JPY 83,418 million). R&D expenses JPY 46,605 million (-18.6%): LSI JPY 21,312 million, Semiconductor Devices JPY 23,778 million.
quarterly_data.figure: capex JPY 82,403 million (-38.1%); R&D JPY 46,605 million (-18.6%)

quarterly_data.signal: Planned capital investment: new and upgraded facilities totalling JPY 60,000 million as of FY2026 year-end. Named plans, all production equipment starting April 2026 and completing March 2027 (capacity increase not stated because the product mix is too diverse): Rohm (Kyoto and other sites) JPY 13,701 million; Lapis Semiconductor (Yokohama and other sites) JPY 21,519 million; Rohm Apollo (Fukuoka) JPY 4,894 million; Rohm Integrated Systems (Thailand) JPY 5,695 million. On April 1, 2026 Rohm Apollo was reorganised into two companies: front-end maker Rohm Device Manufacturing and back-end maker Rohm Assembly Manufacturing.
quarterly_data.figure: planned capex JPY 60,000 million; Lapis Semiconductor JPY 21,519 million; Rohm JPY 13,701 million

quarterly_data.signal: FY2026 product development (company R&D report; industry-leading wording is the company's own claim): RY7P250BM, a 100V power MOSFET for hot-swap circuits in 48V AI server power supplies and for industrial power, combining what the company calls industry-top SOA capability with low on-resistance; HSDIP20, a 4-in-1 / 6-in-1 SiC molded module (750V and 1,200V) for xEV on-board chargers; DOT-247, a 2-in-1 SiC module for PV inverters, UPS and semiconductor relays; AW2K21, a 2.0mm x 2.0mm dual MOSFET for fast charging; an AI microcontroller (ML63Q253x / ML63Q255x) with on-device learning and inference; AEC-Q100 current sense amplifiers for 48V and 5V/12V automotive power; a 1ch high-side IPD for zone ECUs; ESD protection diodes for 10Gbps-plus interfaces; near-infrared LEDs; and the UCR10C shunt resistor.

FY2026 net sales by customer location: Japan JPY 145,144 million, China JPY 146,600 million, other JPY 189,402 million (total JPY 481,148 million). No single customer accounted for 10% or more of net sales, so the major-customer table is omitted.
quarterly_data.figure: China JPY 146,600 million; Japan JPY 145,144 million; no customer at 10% or more
